summary: Feed feed-1 to IDS is degraded: 40.3% of TCP sessions (81/201) are one-way, exceeding 10% threshold. IDS requires bidirectional traffic for stateful inspection and will have severely reduced detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / capture layer is delivering only one direction of bidirectional flows. Most likely asymmetric routing with tap/SPAN on only one path, or broker not aggregating both directions to the same tool output, or hash-based load-balancing splitting client->server and server->client to different tools without symmetric hashing.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_both_directions=true for TCP stream reassembly, state tracking and signature matching. With 40.3% one-way sessions the IDS cannot reconstruct flows, will miss attacks that span both directions, generate incomplete events and suffer high false-negative rate.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires both directions on the same port to correlate request/response. Aggregating both sides of each flow (or enabling symmetric hashing if load-balancing) restores full bidirectional visibility needed for detection.
